Autoimmune inflammation of the brain, spinal cord and surrounding tissues defines CNS lupus; other systemic manifestations are not assumed.
Gastric gas retention with impaired belching, typically following fundoplication, defines this gastrointestinal syndrome.
B-cell lymphoid neoplasm involving marrow and spleen; infiltrative hepatomegaly occurs in 30-79%. Nephropathy and bone lesions are occasional.
Clonal eosinophil disorder; eosinophilic endomyocardial injury affects roughly 30-50% in myeloproliferative series. Other organ frequencies vary.
Severe sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 7/7 reported patients. Sperm abnormalities and infertility are reproductive findings outside the axes.
Factitious psychiatric disorder imposed on another; it does not define damage to a particular organ in the affected caregiver.
Rhabdomyosarcoma located in the oral cavity; muscle differentiation alone does not establish a separate locomotor organ site.
Tumour originates in the esophagus; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine gland disease or hormonal dysfunction.
Umbrella for neoplasms arising in the heart, pericardium or vessels; no other organ is consistently affected across subtypes.
Immune-mediated recurrent arthritis defines the disease. Attacks remit without persistent joint damage; progression to rheumatoid arthritis is separate.
Inherited renal tubular amino acid transport defect with recurrent cystine stones. Hypertension and urinary infections are separate complications.
Hypersensitivity-mediated alveolar and interstitial lung inflammation caused by inhaled mushroom-associated organic antigens.
Carcinoma originates in bronchial epithelium; metastatic sites and paraneoplastic complications are not defining organ involvement.
Acute dysfunction of parasympathetic and sudomotor autonomic nerves; hypohidrosis does not establish intrinsic skin damage.
Perforating dermatosis with abnormal dermal elastic fibers and characteristic hyperkeratotic, serpiginous papules.
Malignant neoplasm of the trachea. Lymphoma is only one subtype and does not justify an immune label for the umbrella.
Vanishing white matter leukodystrophy; ovarian insufficiency reported in 2/2 and cataract in 1/1 patients support involvement, with substantial small-sample uncertainty.
Inherited developmental cataract; the associated adult i blood-group phenotype does not itself cause blood-cell dysfunction.
Hereditary susceptibility is defined by the uveal tumour site; this label does not imply an existing melanoma or current ocular damage.
Mitochondrial disease defined by cataracts and cardiomyopathy; myopathy occurs in 80-99%. Sparse neurologic and haematologic findings omitted under the four-axis cap.
Bilateral optic nerve sheath meningiomas occupy and impair the optic nerves, which belong to the ocular axis.
Gonadal failure and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; hearing loss and learning disability each 30-79%. Thyroiditis, hypertension and steatosis are separate diseases.
Defining dermal lymphatic tumour infiltration causes persistent skin edema and induration. Breast origin has no axis; the name does not indicate immune inflammation.
Skeletal and oral malformations with severe intellectual disability define syndrome; heart defects are defining. Deafness omitted under four-axis cap; reported cases are few.
